Abstract

Complementary experts for heterogeneous future motion

Dynamic scenes contain stationary regions, coordinated motion, local interactions, and articulated trajectories. A single scene-level predictor need not extrapolate every motion regime equally well.

MoRE-GS freezes a Gaussian scene reconstructed only from the observed temporal prefix, forecasts control-keypoint motion with four complementary experts, and combines them using a compact router conditioned on soft motion group and forecast horizon.

The router is calibrated through the frozen renderer on a held-out interval inside the observed prefix. Future frames do not influence reconstruction, grouping, expert fitting, routing, checkpoint selection, or early stopping.

Method

Motion experts routed by group and forecast horizon

The canonical Gaussian representation remains frozen while persistence, coefficient-space, graph-based, and structured predictors forecast future keypoint motion.

Learned routing

Different motion groups prefer different experts

Sixteen soft motion groups and four horizon bins form a 256-parameter routing table, calibrated through the frozen renderer on observed frames only.
